title: DES and why it aged
syllabusUnit: Unit II: Data Encryption Standard & Cryptanalysis
covers: DES, strength of DES, 3DES, differential & linear cryptanalysis (intuition)
learningGoals: You will be able to outline the 16-round architecture of DES.
You will be able to explain why a 56-bit key is vulnerable to modern brute-force.
You will be able to describe how Triple-DES (3DES) encrypts data.

lessonCards.title: The Data Encryption Standard (DES)
lessonCards.analogy: A sturdy 1970s steel bank vault with 16 internal mechanical gear shifts.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Adopted in 1977, DES takes a 64-bit block, applies an Initial Permutation (IP), runs 16 Feistel rounds using eight 6-to-4 bit S-boxes, and ends with IP^-1.
lessonCards.example: DES was standard for global ATM banking networks for over two decades.

lessonCards.title: The 56-bit Key Trap
lessonCards.analogy: A briefcase lock with only 3 dials: secure against thieves on foot, but opened in seconds by a robot.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Although the DES key is 64 bits, 8 bits are parity checks, leaving an effective key of only 56 bits (2^56 ≈ 7.2 × 10^16 keys). In 1998, EFF's Deep Crack machine broke DES in 56 hours.
lessonCards.example: Today, a modern graphics card can exhaust 2^56 keys in under a day.

lessonCards.title: Triple-DES (3DES) & EDE Mode
lessonCards.analogy: Putting three padlocks on a treasure chest: Encrypt with Key 1, Decrypt with Key 2, Encrypt with Key 3.
lessonCards.coreConcept: To extend DES life without rewriting software, 3DES applies Encrypt-Decrypt-Encrypt (EDE): C = E(K3, D(K2, E(K1, P))). Using 3 distinct keys provides 168-bit key length.
lessonCards.example: If K1 = K2 = K3, 3DES falls back to standard single DES for backwards compatibility.

questions.prompt: What is the effective secret key length of the standard Data Encryption Standard (DES)?
questions.explanation: Although DES input keys are 64 bits, 8 bits are parity check bits, leaving exactly 56 bits of true cryptographic entropy.
questions.realWorldExample: In 1999, distributed.net and EFF cracked a DES key in 22 hours and 15 minutes.

questions.prompt: How many Feistel rounds are performed in standard DES encryption?
questions.explanation: DES executes exactly 16 Feistel rounds with sixteen 48-bit subkeys generated from the key schedule.
wrongExplanations: 32 rounds is used in some specialized ciphers.
questions.realWorldExample: Each round uses a 48-bit subkey generated by PC-1, circular left shifts, and PC-2.

questions.prompt: Why does Triple-DES use an Encrypt-Decrypt-Encrypt (EDE) sequence instead of Encrypt-Encrypt-Encrypt (EEE)?
options: Setting K1 = K2 = K3 makes it backwards-compatible with single DES: E(K, D(K, E(K, P))) = E(K, P)
Decryption runs twice as fast as encryption
It makes the ciphertext half the size
questions.explanation: In EDE, when K1=K2, the middle decryption cancels the first encryption, leaving a standard single-DES ciphertext.
wrongExplanations: Correct! EDE provides seamless backwards compatibility with legacy DES hardware.
Decryption uses identical Feistel execution time.
Block cipher output size always equals block size (64 bits).
questions.realWorldExample: Financial payments systems ran 3DES EDE for years before migrating to AES.

questions.prompt: What cryptanalytic technique introduced by Biham and Shamir analyzes how input differences propagate to output differences?
questions.explanation: Differential cryptanalysis studies how specific differences between plaintext pairs lead to predictable differences in intermediate states.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Differential cryptanalysis exploits S-box difference distributions.
Linear cryptanalysis approximates round functions with linear boolean equations.
questions.realWorldExample: IBM knew about differential cryptanalysis in 1974 and hardened DES S-boxes against it 15 years before it was publicly published.

questions.prompt: Why is standard single DES completely prohibited in modern cybersecurity protocols?
options: Its 56-bit key space can be brute-forced in hours by modern compute hardware
It requires internet access to run
questions.explanation: A 56-bit key space (2^56 keys) is far too small; cloud GPU clusters can test all possible keys in hours.
wrongExplanations: Correct! 56-bit keys are obsolete and insecure against brute force.
DES processes raw binary bytes, regardless of character set.
DES is a purely local mathematical algorithm.
questions.realWorldExample: NIST officially withdrew DES as a federal standard in 2005, replacing it with AES.

questions.prompt: Why doesn't Double-DES (running DES twice with two keys: K1, K2) provide 112 bits of security?
options: The Meet-in-the-Middle attack reduces effective security to only 2^57 operations
Keys cancel each other out to 0
questions.explanation: The Meet-in-the-Middle attack encrypts from one side and decrypts from the other, matching intermediate states in a hash table in 2^57 time.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Meet-in-the-Middle proves Double-DES is only slightly stronger than single DES.
Different keys do not cancel to zero.
questions.realWorldExample: This is why 3DES requires three operations (EDE) rather than two.

ashRecap: DES was an engineering marvel with 16 Feistel rounds, but its 56-bit key was too small for modern computing. Always use AES!
